proof_attempt_summary: The derivation established matched estimation and honest-band rates for the stated binary-stratum model, with a same-class lower-bound witness and observable smooth-regime Gaussian and multiplier inference. D0.5 graded the delivered work subfield, below the field floor; an all-law constrained-model efficiency claim failed at binding-envelope laws and was removed from the archived core. The paper did not enter Lean formalization after the below-floor verdict.
tldr: Over the varying full-data law class allowing zero-initiation intervals, the complete causal value map has matched minimax estimation and honest-band orders \(n^{-(1+s)/3}\) below \(s=1/2\), \(\log(n)/\sqrt n\) at the boundary, and \(n^{-1/2}\) above it.  The observable no-division projected estimator and one joint Markov calibration attain these orders, while the finite multiscale witness gives same-class all-procedure lower bounds and transfers those lower bounds to every larger model containing the witness family.  For \(s>1/2\), the explicit constrained spline pilot is uniformly supremum-norm consistent, the projected estimator has a uniform root-sample-size oracle expansion, and the observable multiplier band is uniformly asymptotically exact.
gap: ZhaoYingXu2026 Theorem 1 derives the efficient influence function for a general time-varying multiplier under boundedness and bounded total variation, while its Section 4 verifies Donsker and uniform-inference conditions for a scalar interval and describes a finite-dimensional parametric extension. Generic Hölder empirical-process results do not remove bounded variation for the complete infinite-dimensional multiplier curve or deliver observable causal score replacement, varying-law minimax converses, and honest same-class bands.
fill: An exact drift identity, lifted projected cross-fitted estimator, explicit public-radius rough band, and legal multiscale lower experiment jointly target estimation risk, honest-band width, and smooth-regime efficiency over the same varying law class.
